title: Hearing intervals
summary: Link each interval to a song you already know, so you can name it by ear.

steps.title: Naming what you hear
steps.body:
Learning to name intervals by sound alone, without looking at the keys, is called **ear training**.

**Why it matters:** You already play by ear. Ear training puts names on what you hear, so when the band says "it goes up a 6th" you will recognise it at once.

steps.title: Songs you already know
steps.body:
The opening notes of familiar tunes make handy hooks:

- minor 2nd: the *Jaws* theme
- major 2nd: *Happy Birthday*, from "-py" to "birth"
- minor 3rd: *Greensleeves*
- major 3rd: *Oh When the Saints*
- perfect 4th: *Here Comes the Bride*
- tritone: *The Simpsons* theme
- perfect 5th: *Twinkle Twinkle Little Star*, the jump to the second "twinkle"
- major 6th: *My Bonnie Lies Over the Ocean*
- minor 7th: the original *Star Trek* theme
- octave: *Somewhere Over the Rainbow*

**Why it matters:** a song hook turns an abstract name into a sound you already know. If another song works better for you, use that one.

steps.title: The intervals with a song hook
steps.body: Play each lit key against C and hum its song.

items.prompt: Pick any key and play a perfect 5th up from it. Hum Twinkle Twinkle to check.
Pick any key and play a major 3rd up from it. Hum Oh When the Saints to check.
Pick any key and play a perfect 4th up from it. Hum Here Comes the Bride to check.
Pick any key and play a minor 3rd up from it. Hum Greensleeves to check.
Pick any key and play an octave up from it. Hum Somewhere Over the Rainbow to check.

steps.title: Guess before you look
steps.body: Play any two notes, hum the song that fits, and guess the interval. Then check the name the app shows.
